Node 22 public unscoped and session-scoped reads each preserved 40 fresh pass rows/counts and reduced cold content transport from 40 per-anchor children to one object batch plus one diff-tree chunk; unchanged repeats spawned none.

Integrated public API and contract proof on 7db32699: 40 off-history anchors use one object batch plus one bounded content chunk for unscoped and scoped reads, repeats spawn zero; replacement/graft interpretations rotate coherently, a fetched missing object is retried, SHA-256 stays native, and an 8300-path single anchor splits under record/argv bounds with no partial publication after a controlled later-chunk failure.

OLD behaviour: the read forks one rev-list --count per (anchor, path) — 48 children for the 12-anchor scenario, and 1748 of 1750 git children (15.8s read) at 437-anchor production scale on a real 6197-commit history. Child count scales with anchors x governed paths, which is the defect.
